findings.where: Hero, the whole first screen: arches, the red heading, the one line and the button (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Mark's face does not appear anywhere in this direction, and the tile does not show where his portrait would sit on the stone ground. The only picture is the mark. On first sight the brand is the aqueduct and a carved name, not the man.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer choosing an individual consultant needs to see a real person before writing. Mark would object too: the brief's value 3, 'the man himself, seen and heard', applies to every direction, and this tile answers the 'heard' half only, through the article quote.

findings.where: Hero heading 'MARK · M · MOSELEY / INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR', in full-width monumental red Roman capitals across the first screen
findings.fault: The name is set as a carved public inscription, at a size and formality that reads like a memorial or an institution's dedication. It does not read as an approachable personal advisor. The tone is monumental and impersonal where the brief asks for a person talking.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose voice rule (§5) asks for an approachable individual and against the established-firm register. A bank officer would also form the wrong impression: a grand heritage body, not one experienced lawyer they can simply write to.

findings.where: Hero line under the heading: 'Advice on infrastructure projects and the laws that enable them, from a former Lead Lawyer in the World Bank's PPP Group.'
findings.fault: The first screen says what the practice does and gives one credential. It does not say who the work is for (governments and development agencies) or where it is done (the regions or countries Mark works in). The 5-second test is only half passed.
findings.who_objects: An officer at a regional development bank, who needs to know at once that Mark works for bodies like theirs in their region (first-visit trust items 2 and 6, and 'what a visitor must be sure of' for an advisor).

findings.where: 'WRITE TO MARK' button in the hero (a mailto link), and the page's end below the article specimen and motion sketch, which has no footer
findings.fault: The only contact route is a button that opens a mail client. The email address is never shown in full as text, and no footer carries it on the home page or the article specimen.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a locked-down work machine or using webmail, where clicking mailto does nothing or opens the wrong app. They cannot see or copy the address to forward to a procurement colleague (first-visit trust item 7).

findings.where: Article specimen, the dateline 'MMM INFRA BLOG NO. 8 · 18 SEPTEMBER 2024' under 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'
findings.fault: The article is signed by the firm's blog, not by Mark. No byline names him and there is no one-line bio, so a reader landing on the article from a social post does not learn who wrote it or why to trust him.
findings.who_objects: A reader arriving from Mark's LinkedIn post straight onto the article (item 12, identity on every deep page). Mark would object too, since the brief bans the firm's voice (value 1, 'never a firm's voice').

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge · Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'
findings.fault: The newest talk is listed without its venue or host. Standing by who asked is the strongest proof an advisor has, and this row does not show it.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who judges an individual by who invited them and where. A lecture with no named host or body proves little to them ('Feel the CV': the newest talk with its venue).

findings.where: The whole page: the hero and the article specimen
findings.fault: There is no third-party proof and no slot for it. Apart from the single World Bank line, nothing links out to work that named bodies host (published reports, a bank's page for the lecture), so every claim rests on Mark's own word.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who wants proof they can check before contacting an individual (item 14: with no testimonials held, link out to work that named bodies host; never invent any).
